profiles.name: Abdul-Malik al-Houthi
profiles.reward_text: Financial reward of $30 million for information leading to the arrest or location of Abdul-Malik al-Houthi.
profiles.issuer: Presidency of State Security / Saudi-led Coalition
profiles.dispute_note: Ansar Allah rejects the authority and designations of the Saudi-led coalition, viewing the wanted list and sanctions as aggressive political acts within the context of the Yemeni civil war. Independent analysts treat the listing as part of the broader armed conflict between the opposing factions.
profiles.crimes: Saudi authorities accuse Abdul-Malik al-Houthi of terrorism, leading an illegitimate armed insurgency, threatening regional security, and ordering ballistic missile attacks against Saudi territory.
profiles.summary: Abdul-Malik al-Houthi is the supreme leader of Yemen's Ansar Allah movement. In November 2017, Saudi Arabia placed him first on a published list of 40 wanted Houthi figures, offering a $30 million reward for information aiding his capture.

sources.title: Saudi Press Agency - Coalition Command Announces List of 40 Names of Terrorist Leaders
Reuters - Saudi Arabia offers $30 mln reward for Houthi leader

profiles.name: Nicolás Maduro Moros
profiles.reward_text: The U.S. Department of State offers a reward of up to $15 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Nicolás Maduro Moros.
profiles.dispute_note: The Venezuelan government and official authorities reject the U.S. indictment and bounty, characterizing them as politically motivated, baseless allegations intended to trigger regime change. International legal commentators also note the politically extraordinary nature of a foreign state issuing a reward for a sitting head of state.
profiles.crimes: Accused by the U.S. Department of Justice of narco-terrorism, drug trafficking, corruption, and conspiracy to import cocaine into the United States. The U.S. government alleges he partnered with the FARC and led the 'Cartel of the Suns' trafficking organization.
profiles.summary: Nicolás Maduro is the President of Venezuela, wanted by U.S. authorities under a March 2020 federal indictment for alleged narco-terrorism and drug trafficking. The U.S. Department of State offers a reward of up to $15 million for information leading to his arrest or conviction.

profiles.name: Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes
profiles.position: Leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG)
profiles.reward_text: The U.S. Department of State is offering a reward of up to $10 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Nemesio Oseguera-Cervantes.
profiles.crimes: The U.S. government accuses Oseguera Cervantes of conspiracy to distribute international shipments of cocaine, methamphetamine, and fentanyl into the United States. He is further accused of racketeering activities, firearm offenses, and leading the violent Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG).
profiles.summary: Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, widely known as 'El Mencho,' is the alleged founder and top leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. He is actively wanted by United States law enforcement for large-scale international drug trafficking and racketeering.
profiles.physical: Height approx. 5'8" (173 cm), weight approx. 150 lbs (68 kg), brown eyes, dark hair

profiles.name: Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores
profiles.reward_text: Up to $5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores.
profiles.crimes: The United States government accuses Guerrero Flores of being the supreme leader of Tren de Aragua and conspiracy to engage in racketeering, drug trafficking, human smuggling, and money laundering across the Western Hemisphere.
profiles.summary: Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, widely known as 'Niño Guerrero,' is the alleged head of the Venezuelan transnational criminal group Tren de Aragua. He escaped Tocorón prison in Venezuela in September 2023 and remains an international fugitive.

profiles.name: Jobanis de Jesús Ávila Villadiego
profiles.position: Leader of the Clan del Golfo (Autodefensas Gaitanistas de Colombia)
profiles.reward_text: The U.S. Department of State offers a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Jobanis de Jesus Avila Villadiego.
profiles.crimes: The U.S. Department of State accuses Jobanis de Jesús Ávila Villadiego of conspiracy to distribute international shipments of cocaine intended for illegal importation into the United States. He is alleged to be a top leader of the Clan del Golfo drug cartel, overseeing armed violence and large-scale narco-trafficking operations.
profiles.summary: Jobanis de Jesús Ávila Villadiego, alias 'Chiquito Malo', is a top leader of Colombia's Clan del Golfo cartel. He is wanted by U.S. and Colombian authorities on international drug trafficking charges.

profiles.name: Murat Karayılan
profiles.position: Senior leader within the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) and head of the PKK's People's Defense Forces
profiles.crimes: He is accused of being a senior leader of the PKK, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization, and was designated by the U.S. as a Significant Foreign Narcotics Trafficker. Turkish prosecutors also accuse him of disrupting state unity and territorial integrity, deliberate murder, and committing murder using explosives.
profiles.summary: The U.S. Department of State offers a reward of up to $5 million for information on Murat Karayilan, a senior PKK leader. He is also subject to Turkish detention warrants in connection with murder and terrorism offenses.

profiles.name: Víctor Quispe Palomino
profiles.position: Leader of the Militarized Communist Party of Peru
profiles.reward_text: The U.S. Department of State offers a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Victor Quispe-Palomino.
profiles.crimes: The U.S. Department of State accuses Quispe Palomino of narco-terrorism and international drug trafficking. He is alleged to lead the Militarized Communist Party of Peru, directing illicit cocaine production and armed attacks to support narcotics smuggling activities.
profiles.summary: Víctor Quispe Palomino is the leader of the Militarized Communist Party of Peru, an insurgent remnant of Shining Path operating in the VRAEM region. He is wanted by U.S. and Peruvian authorities for narco-terrorism and drug trafficking.

profiles.name: Adil Öksüz
profiles.position: Former Theology Lecturer, Alleged FETÖ Air Force Imam
profiles.reward_text: Up to 10 million Turkish Lira reward offered under the Red Category of Turkey's Terrorist Wanted List (Terör Arananlar).
profiles.dispute_note: The official Turkish account of the coup attempt and the blanket classification of the Gülen movement as a terrorist organization (FETÖ) are disputed by Gülen, his supporters, and various international observers. Critics and political analysts have also pointed out suspicious circumstances around Öksüz's swift release after his post-coup arrest.
profiles.crimes: Turkish authorities accuse Adil Öksüz of acting as the secret 'Air Force imam' for the Fethullahist Terrorist Organisation (FETÖ/PDY) and serving as a key planner of the July 15, 2016 failed coup attempt. He is charged with attempting to overthrow the constitutional order, membership in an armed terrorist organization, and attempting to assassinate the president.
profiles.summary: Adil Öksüz is a primary suspect in Turkey's 2016 coup attempt accused of managing military conspirators on behalf of Fethullah Gülen. He was detained at Akıncı Air Base immediately following the failed coup but was released by a judge shortly after and subsequently went missing.

profiles.name: Muhammad Sinwar
profiles.position: Senior Commander in the Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades
profiles.reward_text: Israel offered a $300,000 reward for information leading to the location or capture of Muhammad Sinwar.
profiles.dispute_note: Hamas and its supporters regard its military actions as legitimate resistance against Israeli military occupation, contesting the Israeli designation of its commanders as terrorists.
profiles.crimes: Accused by Israeli authorities of involvement in acts of terrorism, senior leadership within the Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades, and participating in the planning and execution of attacks against Israel, including the October 7, 2023 attacks.
profiles.summary: Muhammad Sinwar is a senior commander in Hamas's armed wing, the Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades. In December 2023, the Israeli military dropped reward leaflets in the Gaza Strip seeking information on his whereabouts.

profiles.name: Rabih Alkhalil
profiles.reward_text: A reward of up to $250,000 CAD is offered for information leading to the arrest of Rabih Alkhalil.
profiles.issuer: Royal Canadian Mounted Police / Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of British Columbia / Bolo Program
profiles.crimes: Alkhalil is wanted for escaping lawful custody from the North Fraser Pretrial Centre in July 2022 while on trial for first-degree murder. He was subsequently convicted in absentia of first-degree murder and has prior convictions for murder and large-scale drug trafficking tied to organized crime.
profiles.summary: Rabih Alkhalil is a high-profile Canadian fugitive who escaped from a British Columbia pretrial facility in July 2022. He remains subject to an international Interpol Red Notice and a major Canadian law enforcement reward.
profiles.physical: Height approx. 5 ft 10 in (178 cm), weight approx. 165 lbs (75 kg), brown eyes, black hair, tattoo on left arm.

profiles.name: Igor Girkin
profiles.position: Former FSB officer, former commander of pro-Russian forces in Donetsk
profiles.reward_text: Defence Intelligence of Ukraine guarantees a payment of $100,000 for handing over Igor Girkin (Strelkov) into Ukrainian captivity.
profiles.issuer: Main Directorate of Intelligence of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine (GUR)
profiles.dispute_note: Girkin and Russian authorities do not recognize the jurisdiction or criminal charges brought by Ukrainian or Dutch courts. In July 2023, Girkin was detained by Russian security forces and later sentenced in Russia to four years in prison on domestic extremism charges.
profiles.crimes: Ukrainian authorities accuse Girkin of war crimes, terrorism, unlawful imprisonment, and participation in illegal armed formations in eastern Ukraine. He was also convicted in absentia by a Dutch court for his role in the 2014 downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17.
profiles.summary: Igor Girkin is a Russian former military and intelligence officer who played a key role in the 2014 annexation of Crimea and the conflict in eastern Ukraine. Ukrainian military intelligence offered a $100,000 bounty for his capture and surrender to Ukrainian custody.

profiles.position: Leader of the Yemelyanov Organized Crime Syndicate

profiles.crimes: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia accuses Yemelyanov of creating and managing an organized crime group involved in multiple contract murders, extortion, and illegal weapons trafficking. profiles.reward_text: The Ministry of Internal Affairs offers a reward of 1 million rubles for information assisting in the location and arrest of the suspect.

profiles.crimes: Russian authorities accuse Valery Andreev of kidnapping, raping, and murdering multiple women in the Orenburg Region between 2006 and 2012. He fled law enforcement in 2012 during the investigation and remains one of Russia's most wanted fugitives.
profiles.summary: Valery Andreev, known as the 'Orsk Maniac', is a Russian fugitive wanted for the serial rape and murder of numerous women. He has been on federal and international wanted lists since 2012 with an official reward offered for his capture.
